title: JPMorgan Chase CEO on President Trump, North Korea and China
description: JPMorgan Chase, the nation's largest bank, announced its plans Wednesday to open 70 new branches and hire 700 new employees in the Washington D.C., Virginia and Maryland area. The move is part of the firm's five-year, $20 billion investment supporting economic growth in the region. Jeff Glor spoke with JPMorgan Chase chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon about the expansion, President Trump, immigration and foreign policy. asr.full_text: America's largest bank is making a big investment in the nation's capital. JPMorgan Chase announced plans yesterday to open 70 new branches and hire 700 workers in Washington, D.C., Virginia, and Maryland. It is part of a five-year, $20 billion investment supporting economic growth in the region. CBS Evening News anchor Jeff Gloor spoke with chairman and CEO Jamie Dimon about JPMorgan Chase, President Trump, immigration immigration and a whole lot more. Seventy branches, 700 employees. Big investment here. Why here? Why now? JPMorgan, you know, we have about 5,000 branch on the country. And, you know, because of some regulatory reform, tax reform, we have capital. We want to go and expand. So we've announced we're going to go into 15 new markets and its 700 direct jobs. And why do you want expansion? If you look at the Greater DC Area it is the third-largest market, it one wealthiest market in the country it's all, had some of the poorest neighbourhood. We want help lift them up to wages are up. some bonuses have been given. One of the concerns though is, is that the vast majority a of the benefits from this tax reform has gone to companies and executives and share buybacks. Is that fair? DAN SOUTHERLAND I don't think it's gone to executives, per se. But, like I said, the immediate benefit, there would be immediate benefits for companies are doing right now to help grow and expand in wages and stuff like that. Over time, capital gets reinvested, and that drives productivity and wages. And so the American public has to understand that's what drives it. DAVID BROOKS RAYMONDON The question being that bit, but are the benefits of tax reform right now being distributed, in your estimation, fairly? DAVID BROOKS REYNOLDS Over time they will, but I'd say it can be very hard to do on day 1. But remember, for me to open 500 branches, I need real estate people. I need to train sellers. We need to train branchers. We need to sign leases. So I couldn't do it overnight. DAVID BROOKS REYNOLDS How's President Trump doing? REP. CHRIS KROXIN MULLEN , I'm not going to speak specifically. Regulatory stuff, good. I think a lot of people I speak to as CEOs have seen relief. But let's just reduce the bureaucracy. Which we all know is there. Anyone who deals with government and the DMV or the VA sees it all the time. COLT TAMM- How often do you talk to the president? REP. CHRIS KROXIN MULLEN , Not a lot. COLT TAMM- When you talk to him, what do you say? REP. CHRIS KROXIN MULLEN , Well, I am the chairman of the Business Roundtable. We spoke about trade. We spoke about immigration and about policy issues that were trying to give him our insights on what we think would be good for the country. HARI SREENIVASAN You disagree with him in part on both trade and immigration, but also agree with him in part. JONATHAN CAPEHART Immigration, I don't know, because it's not completely clear where the administration is on the broad spectrum of immigration. I have heard him say publicly, I support DACA. I have heard him say publicly, I want to get immigration reform done. But, of course, it's all wrapped up in border security and things like that. So, I'm not an expert in immigration policy. But, if it were up to me, I'd try to get the immigration fixed. It's tearing at the body of politics. MARK ACKERMAN, There's been a lot of talk about North Korea. We know that Mike Pompeo, outgoing C.A. outgoing CIA director, potentially secretary of state, went to visit Kim Jong-un. The president's really trying to advance that potential summit, which might take place in June. Good idea? DONALD TRUMP, President of the United States of America to Japan": I think it's a great idea. How can trying... To have peace on the Korean Peninsula would be wonderful for the world. And I find it funny when people say don't try. Of course you try. If it doesn't work, it doesn't work. But I think the fact that Pompeo went there is a very good sign and, hopefully that they will come to a resolution. I mean, everyone would want that, including China, Russia, well, hopefully Russia. NICK SCHIFRIN, TVXQ Consultant's CEO, Do you see China as a threat? DAVID WASSERMAN, We should work with them. They do compete economically. And I want to compete with the Chinese banks. But there's no reason we can't do it together and help each other. President Obama has had great relations with President Xi. They should continue that for the sake of the world. LISA DESJARDINS Thank you to Jeff Glor of CBS Evening News.
